channel.title: mint - news
channel.description: Get the latest news and analysis on business, finance, politics from mint, the website of the Mint newspaper, one of India's leading business and financial dailies

item.title: Trump’s warning to Iran: ‘They’ll be hit very hard’ if linked to flydubai plane attack
item.description: Trump made the remarks on Thursday (October 1) as investigators from several countries worked to determine the motive behind the incident involving a FlyDubai Boeing 737 Max 8 that was forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.

item.title: Trump’s next move on Iran? Pentagon weighs carrier, 10,000-troop and Marines deployment to Gulf, report says
item.description: The reported deployments come as major US and Iranian military strikes have entered a lull amid attempts to restart diplomatic negotiations.

item.title: India-US trade talks: Piyush Goyal pushes for early interim deal; US trade chief says sticking points remain
item.description: The two countries are continuing discussions as India seeks terms that allow its exporters to remain competitive in the US market, while Washington pursues its broader trade and tariff objectives.

item.title: Tennessee fails to execute Christa Pike after 2 lethal injections: What happens next as per Tennessee law?
item.description: The failed execution of Christa Pike has raised concerns in Tennessee and beyond. Guv Bill Lee has postponed her execution and ordered a review. Pike's condition remains unclear after a troubling execution attempt on Wednesday, which has sparked legal questions about lethal injection procedures.

item.title: Flydubai incident: Omani pilot suspected of stabbing Captain Smit Machchhar; what are Oman-Israel ties?
item.description: An Omani pilot accused of attacking Flydubai captain Smit Machchhar was on an Israel-bound flight, despite Oman having no formal diplomatic ties with Israel. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu alleged that the attacker had undergone radical Islamist indoctrination.

item.title: FlyDubai flight 'hijack': Who is the co-pilot, and what we know and don't know about his motive
item.description: A FlyDubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv was diverted to Saudi Arabia after the co-pilot allegedly stabbed the captain and attempted to take control of the aircraft. Here's what we know about the incident, the co-pilot, his motive and the ongoing probe.

item.title: No more pink tickets? Delhi women may need ‘Pink Saheli’ smart card for free bus rides from Friday
item.description: The transport department had earlier announced that the smart cards would become mandatory for women passengers seeking free travel on DTC buses from October 1.

item.title: Tajikistan's Rogun Hydropower Project: All about the dam set to become the world's tallest
item.description: The project is already generating electricity even though construction of the dam is still underway. Two of the six planned generating units are operational.

item.title: CJP's Oct 2 Mumbai protest: What are its demands besides Gyanesh Kumar's resignation?
item.description: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) is scheduled to hold a protest in Mumbai on October 2 against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the Election Commission.

item.title: Taylor Swift’s former Beverly Hills home, where she wrote ‘1989’, is up for sale at nearly $8 million: See what’s inside
item.description: Known as the Pillsbury Estate, the property spans about 1.5 acres and was owned by Swift from 2011 to 2018. The singer lived at the home during the period when she was writing her fifth studio album, 1989, which was released in 2014.

item.title: G20 trade ministers reach consensus on food weaponization as Goyal flags food security concerns
item.description: G20 trade ministers agreed on a statement opposing the weaponisation of food through coercive trade actions, with India pushing for a distinction between coercive restrictions and legitimate food-security measures.&nbsp;

item.title: Breast Cancer Awareness Month: Doctors share 5 health tips for working women to reduce risk
item.description: Breast Cancer Awareness Month is here. While there is no guaranteed step to prevent breast cancer, doctors shared five steps women can take to reduce the risk of the deadly disease.&nbsp;

item.title: Mark Zuckerberg, Priscilla Chan donate €150,000 to three Irish GAA clubs: Why they picked these
item.description: The €150,000 donation marks the couple’s support for their new Waterford community, funding sports development and facility upgrades.

item.title: Amarinder Singh Warring resignation: Who will be the next Punjab Congress President? Meet top contenders
item.description: Congress reportedly plans to replace Amarinder Singh Raja Warring as Punjab unit president before 2027 elections. Leadership changes follow an evaluation by Sachin Pilot amid factional tensions, with potential successors including Vijay Inder Singla.

item.title: Trump’s $100,000 H-1B fee blocked again: Relief for Indian IT firms and tech professionals as legal fight continues
item.description: US District Judge Haywood Gilliam in Oakland, California, ruled that US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) and the State Department had failed to follow required rule-making procedures before implementing the fee.

item.title: Flydubai pilot attack, Jet Airways fight and more: 5 unusual cockpit incidents
item.description: Here are some unusual incidents inside aircraft cockpits that have caused trouble for pilots.

item.title: Flydubai incident: Captain Smit Machchhar stabbed, Israel-bound flight diverted to Saudi Arabia — A look at the timeline
item.description: An Omani co-pilot allegedly stabbed the captain and attempted to crash a Flydubai flight, forcing an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. Investigations are ongoing. Captain Smit Machchhar, wounded, managed to assist in restraining the attacker.

item.title: LPU Violence: Founder Ashok Mittal on viral rape rumour, violence and ‘larger conspiracy’ to malign Punjab | Interview
item.description: Ashok Mittal, the founder-chancellor of LPU, says the rape rumours were ‘100 per cent false’ and the whole incident – from provoking social media messages and violence – was part of a larger conspiracy by malicious elements to spread anarchy and destabilise Punjab.

item.title: US has Boeing parts, China has rare earth minerals: How Trump is gaining new leverage in trade talks
item.description: The latest US moves suggest that aviation supply chains could become another bargaining point as Washington and Beijing negotiate over rare earths, tariffs, technology and other areas of economic competition.

item.title: Power prices plunge near zero on exchanges as rains ease demand
item.description: The sudden softening in prices comes as demand eased with cooler weather and the completion of much of the kharif sowing season.

item.title: Govt tightens sugar stock rules to curb hoarding ahead of festivals
item.description: To ensure adequate sugar supply during the festive season, the government has halved stockholding limits for dealers to 1,000 quintals and shortened the holding period to 15 days, effective from 15 October through 30 November.

item.title: UAE probes possible ‘terror’ link in attack on Flydubai flight to Israel that forced Saudi landing | What we know
item.description: The UAE has launched a probe into a Flydubai cockpit attack that forced a Dubai-Tel Aviv flight to divert to Saudi Arabia. Investigators will examine the motive and possible terrorist link after a co-pilot allegedly stabbed the Indian captain and triggered a steep descent.

item.title: ‘Create in India, not just Make in India’: TASL's Murlidharan on next step in defence self-reliance | Exclusive
item.description: India’s defence self-reliance must go beyond manufacturing to designing and owning technology, says TASL CTO R Muralidharan, who flags gaps in high-end chips, sensors and critical materials. He called for a shift from licensed production to designing systems in India.

item.title: FlyDubai passengers recount 'hijacking', 18,000-ft plunge: ‘We saw stabbings, plane felt like rollercoaster’
item.description: Zvika Meness said that the three passengers subdued the attacker and tied him up using his own zip ties and multimedia headphones.

item.title: FlyDubai attack: Hero Captain Smit Machchhar to be honoured with Vishisht Gujarat Garima Award
item.description: Captain Smit Machchhar who thwarted his co-pilot's alleged attempt to crash a Flydubai flight, will be honoured by Gujarat government. The hero captain is being airlifted to Dubai for treatment as he was stabbed by the attacker, as per the latest update by ANI.

item.title: ‘We won Op Sindoor’ by integrating diverse systems: Why India’s military systems must 'talk' to each other | Exclusive
item.description: India's ability to integrate diverse military systems during Operation Sindoor highlighted the need for interoperable defence technology, Dr Jaijit Bhattacharya said. He stressed on open architecture, secure data, adaptable systems, cost-effective counter-drone measures and an AI industrial base.

item.title: Bombay HC orders removal of video targeting SII, Adar Poonawalla, issues notice to defendant: 'Deliberate disobedience'
item.description: The Bombay High Court ordered the removal of a derogatory video by influencer Yohan Tengra that labelled Serum Institute and CEO Adar Poonawalla as mass murderers.

item.title: ‘No force can survive without utilizing AI’: CDS Subramani on why commanders must retain final say in modern warfare
item.description: CDS General Subramani said future warfare will centre on AI, resilient networks and integrated “systems of systems”. He stressed keeping commanders in control of AI decisions, deploying AI at the tactical edge, using digital twins and rapidly scaling defence technology from prototypes to production.

item.title: Watch: Eiffel Tower glows in pink for Octobre Rose — here is why
item.description: Pink October or Octobre Rose is the global name for Breast Cancer Awareness Month, an annual international health campaign observed throughout the month of October.

item.title: Chinese refiners suspend October fuel exports, says report: Which other countries plan curbs amid Iran, Ukraine war
item.description: Sources told Reuters that state ​oil major PetroChina cancelled on Wednesday a handful of its gasoline ⁠and jet fuel shipments that were planned for October.

item.title: What is 200-year-old Nizami sweet that Harsh Goenka is raving about? All to know about ‘Badam ki Jali’
item.description: Harsh Goenka introduced his followers to 'Badam ki Jali'—a 200-year-old Nizami-era delicacy. Describing the intricately patterned and baked confection, he praised the heritage mithai as “soft, nutty, melt-in-the-mouth and not too sweet.”

item.title: ‘Delay is not my problem, as long as…’: Hero pilot Capt Smit Machchhar's eerie foresight months before flydubai stabbing
item.description: Machchhar had also highlighted the immense responsibility that aviation staff shoulder when a flight goes wrong.

item.title: Nationwide NRC push? Why RSS wants it and why Owaisi calls it ‘100 times worse’ than SIR amid Oppn-Gyanesh Kumar row
item.description: Hyderabad MP Owaisi had earlier said that NRC would be '100 times worse' than SIR. The Hyderabad MP alleged that the exercise had already caused immense trouble, particularly to minorities, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes and migrants.

item.title: Brazil election: Can Flavio Bolsonaro challenge Lula in a neck-and-neck race? What latest polls show
item.description: Brazil's presidential election is entering its final stretch, with President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Flavio Bolsonaro in a close first-round race. An AtlasIntel poll gives 45% and Bolsonaro 42%. Voting is set for 4 October, with a runoff on 25 October if required.

item.title: ‘Jerome should be forced to resign’: Trump wants Powell out despite Fed watchdog clearing him | What was the allegation?
item.description: President Trump has urged former Fed Chair Powell to resign over the $2.4 billion renovation of the Fed's headquarters, despite an inspector general report finding no criminal wrongdoing. Management failures and rising costs have sparked controversy around the project and its oversight.
